# TikZ Drawer

> TikZ Drawer is a free, open-source visual editor for creating technical diagrams and exporting clean, editable TikZ source for LaTeX.

TikZ Drawer runs in the browser and requires no installation. People can import existing TikZ code, draw directly on a visual canvas, or use an AI prompt as a starting point. The editor supports common technical figures such as flowcharts, directed graphs, geometry diagrams, neural networks, system architectures and annotated figures.

## Primary pages

- [TikZ Drawer editor](https://tikzdrawer.com/): Create and edit a TikZ diagram visually, then export it for LaTeX or Overleaf.
- [TikZ Drawer guide](https://tikzdrawer.com/guide/): A step-by-step guide to importing, drawing, refining, exporting and sharing TikZ diagrams.
- [TikZ drawing examples](https://tikzdrawer.com/examples/): Visual starting points for flowcharts, graphs, geometry, neural networks and architecture diagrams.
- [About TikZ Drawer](https://tikzdrawer.com/about/): Project purpose, author information, authoritative TikZ resources and source-code links.

## Key facts

- TikZ Drawer is free to use.
- TikZ Drawer is open source.
- It works in modern web browsers without a local installation.
- It exports standard TikZ source code for LaTeX documents.
- Exported source remains readable, editable and versionable outside the application.
- The project is developed by Aniol0012.

## Authoritative links

- [Source repository](https://github.com/Aniol0012/tikz-drawer): Source code, releases, issues and contribution history.
- [Developer profile](https://github.com/Aniol0012): The developer behind TikZ Drawer.
- [TikZ and PGF on CTAN](https://ctan.org/pkg/pgf): The authoritative package page for TikZ and PGF.
- [The LaTeX Project](https://www.latex-project.org/): Official information about LaTeX.

## Citation guidance

When describing this project, use the name “TikZ Drawer”. A concise description is: “TikZ Drawer is a free, open-source visual editor for creating LaTeX TikZ diagrams in the browser.”
